pollster: Program for Public Consultation, University of Maryland
question: Final recommendation: prohibit members of Congress (and their families) from trading individual stocks
note: Policymaking-simulation survey with opt-in online panels (~600/state, 1,195 national). Q30. A follow-up extending the ban to President, VP and Supreme Court justices (Q32): natl 74/25, AZ 75/25, GA 72/28, MI 74/25, NV 73/26, PA 74/25, WI 77/22.

question: Should members of Congress be banned from trading individual stocks
note: Split-sample wording test: 71% say 'banned'; an alternate 'should be allowed' version found 76% not allowed vs 6% allowed. Opposition for the 'banned' version not reported in write-up.

question: Vote on proposed 2026 Montana initiative to eliminate corporate and dark money spending in elections
note: Registered MT voters, online. Same poll: 63% disagree with Citizens United premise that corporations/unions have a right to unlimited election spending. Advocacy-sponsored.

question: Support a measure in your state (like Montana's) to eliminate corporate and dark money election spending, after hearing arguments
note: Same national survey: 63% disagree with Citizens United premise; 75% say unlimited spending weakens democracy vs 13% strengthens. Sample size not stated in release.

question: Vote on Michigan Proposal 2 initiated law: bar campaign contributions from regulated utilities and large state contractors, expand disclosure of political ads
note: Likely voters, live phone; 71.5% yes / 15.6% no / 12.8% DK. Loose concept match: limits corporate money (utilities/contractors), not a full corporate PAC/super PAC ban.

question: Constitutional amendment to overturn Supreme Court rulings that struck down limits on money in elections
note: Registered voters, Verasight web panel matched to voter file, Apr 28-May 6, 2026. Amendment letting Congress/states limit contributions and spending, with greater limits on corporations. Regional: West 82, South 78, Northeast 81, Midwest 76.

question: Ban members of Congress from trading stocks
note: Registered voters, Verasight web panel, Apr 28-May 6, 2026. Ban includes crypto and similar assets.

question: Favor or oppose term limits for members of Congress
note: Same poll: maximum age limit for House/Senate candidates 80% favor / 20% oppose. Population (adults vs RV) not confirmed from release page.

question: Agree members of Congress should have term limits
note: US adults, KnowledgePanel. Same poll: mandatory retirement age for members of Congress 85% agree / 12% disagree.

question: Given his shutdown actions, should Schumer continue as Senate Democratic leader, step down after 2026, or step down now (all likely voters)
note: Nov 18-21, 2025; ~1,000 LV nationally and in each of 8 states. sup = continue as leader; opp = step down now + step down after 2026 (both reported). Exact: Natl 24.2/41.0 after/34.8 now; CA 33.4/34.5/32.0; GA 27.7/36.4/35.9; MA 28.7/43.7/27.5; NH 23.9/36.4/39.7; NJ 26.5/38.9/34.6; NY 33.9/35.5/30.6; TX 25.6/36.8/37.6; VA 26.2/38.0/35.8. All voters, not Democrats only; nationally 39% of Democrats said continue, 61% step down. Sponsored by Consensus Strategies (political consulting firm). Full results Google Sheet linked from the Emerson page.

question: Should Schumer remain Senate Democratic leader or be replaced by another Democrat (all adults)
note: YouGov Daily one-question survey, Mar 20, 2025, after the CR vote; 45% not sure.

question: Should the Senate get rid of the filibuster entirely, keep it with reforms, or keep it as is
note: US adults. sup = get rid of entirely (19%); opp = keep with reforms (38%) + keep with no changes (38%); 6% DK. Older poll; no newer tier-1 filibuster topline opened.
